verdicts.why: In A.K.A. The Perfect Burger Vido visits Jessica to hear about her latest heroics (flying to Mexico), then asks her to come to dinner, which she cannot. Text and card lines are accurate.

value.title: Secret Invasion#2
value.text: In 1997, Soren is the first Skrull to take Fury's pledge to spy for him in exchange for his promise to find her people a new home, and Fury thanks her for her courage.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Talos' wife, the first to take Fury's pledge.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The spymaster whose pledge Soren is first to take.

verdicts.why: The scene is right, but Fury's deal is not refuge on Earth: he promises that he and Carol will find the Skrulls a new home while they keep his home safe. Only the text is changed.

In The Series Finale Agatha frees every Westview resident at once to turn them on Wanda. She never addresses or deals with Sharon in particular, so it is a town-wide effect, not an exchange between the two.

value.title: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law#2
value.text: Bruce tells Jen that Blonsky sent him a haiku a while back and the two made up, so he is fine with her taking Blonsky's parole case.
value.on_a_card_about_b: The Abomination, who makes up with Bruce by sending him a haiku.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The man Blonsky makes amends with by sending him a haiku.

verdicts.why: In Superhuman Law Bruce says Blonsky sent him a haiku and they made up. That is a clear reconciliation, so enemy no longer fits. Their later brawl comes from a misreading and is rewritten away, which fits rival better than enemy. Use the tie's actual She-Hulk title string if it differs.

The show shares continuity with the films (set after Trinity). In Sacrifice, a 1977 flashback shows young Whistler; Officer Flannigan introduces Eric's father to him, Whistler tests the boy, and Eric ends up in his care. Mentor fits.
